target_customer: Hospitals, oncology labs and clinicians who would run CTC isolation and analysis for cancer diagnosis and treatment monitoring
problem: Circulating tumor cells are rare in blood and hard to isolate, so cancer is often found late and treatment response is hard to track without invasive biopsies.
business_model: Medical device and consumables (CytoCatch isolation platform and imaging system) sold to labs and clinics; regulatory approval pending

founders.name: Liza Velarde
prior_employers: Zen Fluidics product line development, per YC page
education: International business graduate, university not named (Cartier Women's Initiative profile)
founders.background_notes: Cartier profile says she was still at university when the co-founders approached her. YC page says she led development of the Zen Fluidics microfluidic product line.

founders.name: Alejandro Abarca-Blanco
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder on the YC page. Background not found.

founders.name: Juan Felipe Yee De Leon
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder on the YC page. Background not found.

competitors.name: Cynvenio
competitors.what: Liquid biopsy system capturing CTCs on a microfluidic chip for molecular analysis

technical_complexity.rationale: A microfluidic device plus imaging that isolates rare cells from blood, needing clinical validation and FDA approval, which is hardware and regulatory heavy for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Device IP and eventual regulatory approval could protect it, but a 2014 OncLive piece counted at least 30 firms developing CTC technology and approval is not confirmed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. Menarini acquired CellSearch from Janssen in 2017 per a search summary, strengthening an incumbent.

market_need_then: Liquid biopsy was a crowded research field. Founders say they were driven by losing family and friends to cancer; no dated spend figures found. Pre-sales of $1.2M were claimed in a March 2019 profile.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-driven around early cancer detection; product branded CytoCatch

brand_strength.rationale: No brand-focused coverage found; the name has no sourced meaning and little recognition outside the YC and crowdfunding audience.

outcome_analysis: Delee is a Monterrey-founded device startup that has stayed small through YC, a Heineken-linked donation for its prototype and a crowdfunded round, with no priced institutional round verified. Early patient tests were underway in 2019 and the product still needed clinical trials and FDA approval. The most recent dated activity found is a 2023 summit appearance, so progress to market is unproven.
notes: Funding not verified: aggregators report over $1.3M (Republic listing), $2.3M (Wellfound) and $3.02M (CB Insights), and a Republic crowdfunding offer at a $22.0M valuation; none cross-checked by press, so no round recorded. KingsCrowd fetch returned 403 and was not worked around. Cartier profile (updated Mar 2019) says Heineken CEO donated funds for the first prototype, amount not stated, and pre-sales of $1.2M, while other pages say $1.4M. Competitor list has one entry because only the 2014 OncLive overview was dated near the period; Vortex, Epic Sciences and CellSearch surfaced without dated sources. Headquarters conflict: YC says Monterrey, CB Insights says Sunnyvale after the company moved after YC. Completeness pass: Cross-check found no dated round; totals are company-affiliated and aggregator figures only, so the funding gap is known.
